Review the day

Overview

A day of practical AI, shaped around business.

Most founders have already experimented with basic AI tools. What is missing is the bandwidth to test use cases, separate noise from value, and build real systems. That is what we accomplish in a single day.

We move through four distinct blocks using a straightforward tag team approach. Carlton sets up the foundational strategy, including prompt design and practical AI governance. Jayson immediately demonstrates how to apply it, walking through active systems built on real business data. By the end of the day, you leave with a deeper working knowledge of AI and a clear path forward.

Built just for your group

Designed for business owners who want practical knowledge and working tools.

We begin where you are

Some of you are already deep in the tools. The day starts where the group is with AI and moves quickly. The group won't sit through information they're already past.

Show, don't tell

Every concept arrives as a live demonstration on grounded business problems: field data, spreadsheets, email, scheduling. Seeing it run is the point.

Tailored a month out

A short survey in early September maps each member's current AI use, priorities, and the problems worth solving.

Candid by design

A useful, candid working day: grounded examples, honest caveats about what's hard, and a clear next step each member can take back to the business.

The day

Principle, then practice, four times.

The day runs in four blocks: two each half, each one packed with current information and use cases. Each block opens with the principles then we move deeper into demos. About 50 minutes of work each hour, ten to breathe. Lunch in the middle of the day.

Morning

Blocks 01 · 02 8:00 – 12:00
01The AI-first operating mindset
The principle

Your survey results open the day: who's using what, and what each business wants from it. Then the foundation: putting AI into real decisions, and the habits that change how an owner decides, plans, and executes.

In practice

The same mindset, applied: solve one real problem with an AI tool, and the rest of the skill set grows from there. We work a problem out of your own business together in the room, so you leave with a method you can run again.

02Prompting, research, and every mode of working
The principle

Better questions, real context, and reviewing output before you trust it. Text, voice, documents, images, and data, and where each mode earns a place, demonstrated across ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, and NotebookLM.

In practice

The same methods, run live on business-shaped problems: transcription that becomes follow-up, document and data analysis, and a plain spreadsheet turned into a working dashboard view in front of you.

Lunch, and the conversations that usually turn out to be the best part

Afternoon

Blocks 03 · 04 1:00 – 5:00
03Agents and working systems
The principle

What an agent actually is, where one fits in a company your size, what it should never touch, and the caution that matters: the tool works for you, not the other way around.

In practice

Working agents, live: a standup agent that reviews your day and preps tomorrow (voice in, plan out), field voice reports that become labor records and nightly exception alerts, and email drafted for your approval with a human in the loop.

04Leadership, adoption, and your next system
The principle

Leading adoption instead of watching it happen: internal champions, clear guardrails, safe use, and why it stalls without the CEO in the room.

In practice

What next looks like for each of you: an owner's dashboard you can question in plain English, an honest accounting of what data access and implementation really take, and the proposal page you're reading right now. Its template goes home with you.

Close with open Q&A, next steps, and learning resources worth your time

What you leave with

Value you take back with you.

  1. A clear map of where AI does real work in your businessNot everywhere. The specific places it pays off for a company your size.
  2. Prompting and research approaches you can use the same dayPractical methods for asking better questions and trusting the answers you act on.
  3. Working examples of workflows, dashboards, tools and agentsSeen live, on real business data, with the architecture explained in plain English.
  4. A leadership framework for intentional adoptionChampions, guardrails, and a culture that makes adoption stick.

Your presenters

Who you spend the day with.

Carlton Davis

Carlton Davis Consulting

Carlton Davis

Founder, Carlton Davis Consulting · AI Workshops & Training

Carlton started on Music Row with a decade at Capitol Records, and has spent the years since running companies: COO across software, logistics, engineering, and publishing, leading teams from 10 to 600 and scaling businesses from startup past $85 million. When generative AI arrived in 2022, he treated it the way an operator treats any new tool: put it to work, keep what earns its place.

Now he teaches executives and owners to do the same, as a daily thought partner for how leaders think, decide, and perform. He mentors founders at the Nashville Entrepreneur Center and serves on the Nashville Chamber of Commerce AI Innovation Committee. The tech stays simple; the results don't.

Jayson Rivas

Founder, Impact Consulting · Owner, JHR Photography

Jayson learned force multiplication where it isn't a metaphor: 21 years as a U.S. Army Green Beret, where a small team either builds systems that multiply its effect, or fails. He retired in 2023 and pointed that discipline at his own companies first, then at AI as the tools matured. In a couple of years, a one-person photography business doing under $100K grew into a multi-six-figure family of brands, still run by one or two people, with AI agents working behind every site and workflow.

The same systems now run for clients: voice-driven field reporting for a construction firm, a blueprint takeoff application, a national nonprofit platform. Nothing he teaches came out of a book. It runs his businesses today, which is how a father of six (grandfather of two, private pilot) keeps his weekends.
